beats.label: S1 · Powers arrive
beats.text: Mark Grayson's Viltrumite powers finally emerge at seventeen, and his father Nolan — Earth's mightiest hero Omni-Man — begins training him in secret.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the father-son mentorship whose betrayal is the engine of every future season.

beats.label: S1 · The Guardians die
beats.text: Nolan ambushes and murders the entire Guardians of the Globe, but is left unconscious from their resistance and taken in by the Global Defense Agency as the sole survivor.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The central mystery of the season and the crime that will eventually expose Nolan.

beats.label: S1 · Suspicion closes in
beats.text: Demon detective Damien Darkblood is hired to solve the massacre and quickly circles Nolan, while GDA director Cecil Stedman quietly reaches the same conclusion.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cecil's private knowledge shapes his posture toward the Graysons for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Debbie learns the truth
beats.text: Debbie discovers Nolan's blood-soaked suit; costume-maker Art secretly tests it and confirms her worst fear — her husband killed the Guardians.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Debbie's private knowledge, kept while she still lives with Nolan, is the emotional core carrying into S2.

beats.label: S1 · Battle Beast
beats.text: A brutal beating from Battle Beast leaves Mark hospitalised for a week and exposes how outmatched he still is against real Viltrumite-tier threats.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frames the power gap Mark spends every later season trying to close.

beats.label: S1 · Chicago
beats.text: Nolan reveals himself as a Viltrumite conqueror sent to soften Earth for empire and beats Mark nearly to death through Chicago when Mark refuses to join him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The show's foundational trauma; every future beat between the two men refers back to this fight.

beats.label: S1 · Nolan flees, warning arrives
beats.text: Unable to kill his son, Nolan flees Earth in tears; alien scout Allen warns Mark that the Viltrum Empire will send more once they realise Nolan abandoned his post.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the two open threads S2 opens on: where Nolan is, and the empire's coming response.

cliffhanger.text: Nolan has fled Earth after nearly beating his own son to death, revealing himself as a Viltrumite conqueror. Debbie's marriage was a lie, Chicago lies in ruins, and Allen has warned that the empire will not simply let this go.
questions: Will Nolan ever come back — and as what?
How can a wounded Earth possibly stand against the Viltrum Empire?
Can Mark carry his father's legacy without becoming him?

characters.name: Mark Grayson / Invincible
characters.line: Seventeen-year-old newly-powered hero, beaten near death by his own father and grieving the man he thought Nolan was.

characters.name: Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man
characters.line: Revealed as a Viltrumite conqueror; fled Earth in tears after failing to kill Mark.

characters.name: Debbie Grayson
characters.line: Mark's mother, who has learned her entire marriage was a lie but is publicly grieving a 'dead' husband.

characters.name: Cecil Stedman
characters.line: Director of the GDA; covering up Nolan's true identity to protect Mark, the public, and himself.

characters.name: Atom Eve / Samantha Wilkins
characters.line: Mark's superpowered classmate; quit the Teen Team to use her powers on direct humanitarian work.

characters.name: Amber Bennett
characters.line: Mark's girlfriend, who now knows he is Invincible and has reconciled with him after Chicago.

characters.name: Allen the Alien
characters.line: Coalition of Planets agent who has just delivered the warning that Viltrumites are coming for Earth.

characters.name: The Immortal
characters.line: Original Guardians leader, killed twice by Nolan and now recuperating under GDA protection.

characters.name: Robot / Rudy Connors
characters.line: Teen genius handed the reformed Guardians; secretly running his own long game with a cloned body in progress.

beats.label: S2 · Angstrom's accident
beats.text: A month after Nolan's flight, Angstrom Levy fuses memories from his multiversal variants in a botched experiment, leaving him deformed and blaming Mark.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's villain and the personal grudge that returns in later seasons.

beats.label: S2 · The family cracks
beats.text: Mark buries himself in Invincible work to escape Nolan's shadow, worsening the rift with Debbie, who is unravelling under constant reminders of her husband.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Debbie's grief arc and Mark's avoidance drive the whole season's home life.

beats.label: S2 · Thraxa
beats.text: An alien distress call brings Mark to the planet Thraxa, where he finds Nolan alive, remarried to Andressa, and raising an infant half-brother.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First reunion since Chicago; the discovery of the half-brother reshapes the Grayson family permanently.

beats.label: S2 · Kregg's ultimatum
beats.text: Viltrumites attack Thraxa, capture Nolan for execution, and General Kregg orders Mark to conquer Earth for the empire or watch it burn — but Nolan first shows genuine remorse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Mark on a Viltrumite deadline and finally cracks the door open between father and son.

beats.label: S2 · Home with Oliver
beats.text: Mark returns to Earth with the half-brother; Debbie names him Oliver and chooses to raise him, then Mark breaks up with Amber as Eve's feelings resurface.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the two most important S3 relationships: Debbie–Oliver and Mark–Eve.

beats.label: S2 · Angstrom, and a future confession
beats.text: Angstrom kidnaps Debbie and Oliver to draw Mark into a multiverse-spanning fight; enraged, Mark pummels him nearly to death, and a future Eve then confesses her love.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Mark's first true loss of control and the seed of his and Eve's relationship — both drive S3 directly.

beats.label: S2 · Prison alliance
beats.text: In a distant Viltrumite prison, Nolan admits his guilt to fellow inmate Allen and misses Debbie, laying the groundwork for an alliance against the empire.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The offworld thread S3 opens on and the origin of Nolan's turn from empire.

cliffhanger.text: Mark has beaten Angstrom nearly to death and glimpsed a future in which he loves Eve, but he cannot yet say it out loud. Light-years away, his father sits in a Viltrumite prison finally admitting he was wrong, and a fellow inmate is quietly offering him a way out.
questions: Can Nolan and Allen escape the empire and reach Mark?
Will Mark act on the feelings the future Eve confessed?
Is Angstrom truly gone, or just healing somewhere?

characters.name: Mark Grayson / Invincible
characters.line: Shaken by nearly killing Angstrom, single again, and carrying a confession from a future Eve he can't repeat to the present one.

characters.name: Debbie Grayson
characters.line: Raising Nolan's half-Thraxan son as her own and finally cutting Nolan out of her life.

characters.name: Oliver
characters.line: Mark's infant half-brother from Thraxa; ages fast and is being raised on Earth by Debbie.

characters.name: Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man
characters.line: Viltrumite prisoner awaiting execution; has admitted his guilt and is bonding with Allen.

characters.name: Allen the Alien
characters.line: Captured by the Viltrumites and now pitching Nolan an alliance against the empire.

characters.name: Cecil Stedman
characters.line: GDA director whose methods — Reanimen, secret revivals, hidden ops — are becoming a moral line for Mark.

characters.name: Atom Eve / Samantha Wilkins
characters.line: Mark's teammate and unspoken love; a version of her from the future has just told him she loves him.

characters.name: Angstrom Levy
characters.line: Multiversal genius, deformed by his own experiment and blaming Mark; beaten but not confirmed dead.

characters.name: Robot / Rudy Connors
characters.line: Guardians member now inhabiting a real cloned body; running the team while Immortal steps back.

beats.label: S3 · Training under Cecil
beats.text: Three months after Angstrom, Mark trains under Cecil for the coming Viltrumites; Eve has rejected him after he let slip that a future version of herself confessed her love.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets Mark's stance at season open: still Cecil's weapon, still avoiding Eve.

beats.label: S3 · The Cecil rupture
beats.text: Mark learns Cecil is using Darkwing II and Sinclair's Reanimen; Cecil triggers a pain implant hidden in Mark's head, and Mark severs ties as the Guardians fracture.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Mark's professional relationship with the GDA and splits Earth's hero infrastructure in two.

beats.label: S3 · Two prisons opened
beats.text: Mark and Eve finally start a relationship on Earth; light-years away, Allen breaks out of the Viltrumite prison and frees Nolan with Battle Beast's help.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two threads that converge to open S4: the Grayson–Wilkins couple and Nolan's return to play.

beats.label: S3 · Oliver kills the Maulers
beats.text: Oliver debuts as a hero and kills the Mauler Twins without hesitation, echoing Nolan's philosophy and worrying Mark about the brother he is raising.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Oliver's willingness to kill, which pressure-tests Mark's own line all through S3 and S4.

beats.label: S3 · Invincible War
beats.text: Angstrom returns with evil Invincible variants; heroes die, Rex sacrifices himself to save Robot, and Mark nearly beats Angstrom to death before he escapes.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The heaviest casualty event of the series so far and the moment Mark's restraint fully breaks.

beats.label: S3 · Conquest
beats.text: Aged Viltrumite envoy Conquest arrives to inspect Mark's progress and, disappointed, brutalises Mark and Oliver until Eve's reawakened power lets Mark seemingly kill him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First on-Earth Viltrumite showdown and the reason Eve's powers, Mark's confidence, and Cecil's plans all shift for S4.

beats.label: S3 · Mark hardens
beats.text: Cecil secretly imprisons the comatose Conquest for interrogation, and Mark, hardened by the war, tells Oliver he was right to kill and vows to do the same for family.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Mark endorses Oliver's Viltrumite ethic; this is the Mark who walks into S4 willing to kill Rus.

cliffhanger.text: Angstrom's assault has left Rex dead and Earth's hero ranks gutted, an unconscious Conquest sits in a secret GDA cell, and Mark has just told Oliver that killing is now on the table. Meanwhile Angstrom has been fully healed and is plotting his next move with the Technicians, and mysterious aliens have taken Battle Beast.
questions: How much of Nolan's ruthlessness has Mark just given himself permission to inherit?
What will Cecil learn from a captive Viltrumite?
Who has taken Battle Beast, and what do they want with him?

characters.name: Mark Grayson / Invincible
characters.line: Hardened by Conquest, freshly with Eve, and no longer taking orders from Cecil.

characters.name: Atom Eve / Samantha Wilkins
characters.line: In a relationship with Mark; her body-reconstructing powers have just reawakened at full strength.

characters.name: Oliver
characters.line: Full-fledged hero who has already killed and sees no problem with it — Mark now backs him.

characters.name: Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man
characters.line: Free from the Viltrumite prison with Allen and Battle Beast, en route to the Coalition.

characters.name: Allen the Alien
characters.line: Broke Nolan out and now positioned as a leader of the coming anti-Viltrumite war.

characters.name: Cecil Stedman
characters.line: Severed from Mark; secretly holding Conquest and continuing to operate with methods Mark rejects.

characters.name: Debbie Grayson
characters.line: Has moved on with her new partner Paul, aware of every superhero identity in the family.

characters.name: Angstrom Levy
characters.line: Fully healed by the Technicians and plotting a new world with them — still very much at large.

characters.name: Robot / Rex Sloan
characters.line: Has taken the dead Rex Splode's real name in his honour and continues to lead the fractured Guardians.

beats.label: S4 · The Sequid cost
beats.text: Mark reels from Angstrom and Conquest as the Sequids attempt another invasion; he reluctantly kills their final human host Rus Livingston to end the threat.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First on-page kill of an innocent host — the moral weight Mark carries through the rest of the season.

beats.label: S4 · Recruitment and a secret
beats.text: Nolan and Allen return to Earth to enlist Mark in the Coalition's war on Viltrum; Eve learns she is pregnant but keeps it secret rather than burden his departure.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Two payloads on one departure: the war Mark leaves for and the pregnancy he never learns about.

beats.label: S4 · Conquest, again
beats.text: En route to Talescria, Conquest ambushes their ship and disembowels Mark, who strangles him to death — his first outright Viltrumite kill.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Proves to Mark and the empire that he can kill their own; also puts him out for months.

beats.label: S4 · Viltrum falls
beats.text: After two months of Nolan nursing Mark back to health, the Coalition strikes Viltrum itself and Space Racer's cannon collapses the empire's homeworld into its core.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The empire loses its literal home; the entire endgame of the season pivots on this.

beats.label: S4 · Thragg spares them
beats.text: Thragg still wins the day, beheading Thaedus and disembowelling Nolan, but spares the Graysons because the Viltrumites can afford no further losses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kills the Coalition leader, wounds Nolan, and establishes Thragg as the surviving apex Viltrumite.

beats.label: S4 · Return, and Thragg's offer
beats.text: Back on Earth, Eve tearfully reveals she aborted the pregnancy alone; Thragg then intercepts Mark and warns that surviving Viltrumites are hiding among humans, breeding.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's two closing shocks — the personal loss and the demographic threat now hiding inside Earth.

beats.label: S4 · The Scourge Virus
beats.text: A posthumous message from Thaedus reaches Allen with the perfected Scourge Virus and instructions to unleash it on the hidden Viltrumites — even if humans die too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Loads the moral trigger for whatever war opens the next season.

cliffhanger.text: The Coalition has broken Viltrum but not the Viltrumites. Thragg has told Mark the remaining pure-bloods now live secretly among humans as breeding stock, and Allen holds a virus that could kill them all — and possibly every human alive alongside them.
questions: Will Allen unleash the Scourge Virus knowing the human cost?
Can Mark and Eve rebuild after her secret abortion?
Where are the hidden Viltrumites, and how many part-human children already exist?

characters.name: Mark Grayson / Invincible
characters.line: Traumatised by killing Rus and Conquest, hallucinating Thragg murdering the people he loves, and grieving a child he never knew he was going to have.

characters.name: Atom Eve / Samantha Wilkins
characters.line: Terminated her pregnancy alone during the war; her relationship with Mark is intact but fragile.

characters.name: Nolan Grayson / Omni-Man
characters.line: Gravely wounded by Thragg and disgraced from Viltrum; back on Earth but no longer welcome anywhere.

characters.name: Oliver
characters.line: Fought on Viltrum and survived; now on Talescria with Debbie for a visit.

characters.name: Allen the Alien
characters.line: New leader of the Coalition, holding the perfected Scourge Virus and the choice of whether to use it.

characters.name: Thragg
characters.line: Viltrumite Grand Regent, apex survivor, and architect of the plan to breed a new empire hidden inside humanity.

characters.name: Debbie Grayson
characters.line: Has moved in with Paul and is visiting Oliver offworld.

characters.name: Cecil Stedman
characters.line: Still runs Earth's defence apparatus and is openly wary of Nolan's return.

characters.name: Angstrom Levy
characters.line: Status unknown this season — no update given.
